questions.html:
Suppose that the probability of making a mistake on your homework depends on how much sleep you got the previous night. The probabilities are as follows:

  • If you got at least $8$ hours of sleep, there is a $10 \%$ chance of making a mistake.
  • If you got between $6$ and $8$ hours of sleep, there is a $40 \%$ chance of making a mistake.
  • If you got less than $6$ hours of sleep, there is a $75 \%$ chance of making a mistake.

Additionally, the probabilities for the amount of sleep are:

  • There is a $20 \%$ chance that you got at least $8$ hours of sleep.
  • There is a $50 \%$ chance that you got between $6$ and $8$ hours of sleep.

What is the overall probability that you make a mistake on your homework?
questions.solution:
Answer: C

questions.html: Consider a scenario where a ball is randomly placed in one of $n$ boxes, each with probability $P_{i}$ for box $i$. If the ball is in box $i$, a search of that box will uncover it with probability $\alpha_{i}$. The conditional probability that the ball is in box $j$, given that a search of box $i$ did not uncover it, is:

options.html: $P($ ball in box $j \mid$ not found in box $i)=\frac{P_{j}}{1-\alpha_{i} P_{i}}$, if $j \neq i$
$P($ ball in box $j \mid$ not found in box $i)=\frac{\left(1-\alpha_{i}\right) P_{i}}{1-\alpha_{i} P_{i}}$, if $j \neq i$
$P($ ball in box $j \mid$ not found in box $i)=\frac{1-\alpha_{i} P_{i}}{P_{j}}$, if $j \neq i$
$P($ ball in box $j \mid$ not found in box $i)=\frac{P_{i}}{1-\alpha_{i}}$, if $j \neq i$

questions.solution:
Answer: A

Is it possible to have events $A, B, C$ such that:

$$
P(A \mid C)<P(B \mid C) \text { and } P\left(A \mid C^{c}\right)<P\left(B \mid C^{c}\right) \text {, yet } P(A)>P(B) \text { ? }
$$

options.html: Yes, it is possible, but only if $P(C)=P\left(C^{c}\right)$.
Yes, it is always possible, irrespective of $P(C)$ being equal to $P\left(C^{c}\right)$.
No, it is not possible; such a scenario contradicts probability rules.
The answer cannot be determined from the information given.

questions.solution:
Answer: C
